chunks: Then after them a new generation inherited the Book. They took to the things of this base world, and said: 'We shall (surely) be forgiven this.' Yet they will accept similar things if they came their way again. Had they not been covenanted in the Book to say nothing in the name of God but the truth? And they have read this in it. The abode of the life to come is better for those who fear God. Can they not comprehend?
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about those who inherited the Book but focused on worldly gains?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the spiritual decay of those who inherited the Torah but corrupted its message by prioritizing worldly gain (arad) over divine truth, despite their scholarly knowledge. It underscores the covenant (mithaq) of truthfulness and serves as a warning that intellectual familiarity with Scripture does not guarantee salvation without piety (taqwa). The conclusion challenges the reader to use reason (aql) to distinguish between transient material rewards and the eternal abode of the righteous.
